question: Heparin is the commonly used anticoagulant in cardiac surgery. All of the following are true about heparin except-

options.opa: Weakest acid found in living things
options.opb: Most commercial preparations of heparin now utilize pig intestinal slimes

analysis: Heparin is a widely used anticoagulant that works by activating antithrombin, which in turn inhibits thrombin and factor Xa, thus preventing clot formation. It is known to cause thrombocytopenia in some cases, a condition known as heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Most commercial heparin is derived from pig intestinal mucosa. However, heparin is not classified as the weakest acid found in living things; this statement is incorrect.
